_readme: REQUIRED-FENCE REGISTRY — the inverse of tools/retired-claims.json (check C1).
retired-claims.json catches a BANNED claim REAPPEARING. This catches a REQUIRED
safeguard GOING MISSING — the compression-drift failure this repo records over and
over: an essay says 'X is true, but only in this fenced sense', and the card /
mastery page / daily-arg keeps X and drops the fence, so a sentence that was safe in
the essay reads as heresy on its own screen.
Each rule says: these FILES make a claim that REQUIRES a fence, so each of them must
contain at least one of the `require` patterns (case-insensitive regexes, matched
against the raw served text — fences live in prose AND in card/ARG_PREMISES script
strings, so nothing is stripped). A file with none of them has dropped the fence.
DISCIPLINE (identical to every other net here): a rule must pass on ALL current
content with ZERO gaps before it ships — a guard that fires on our own fenced pages
gets ignored. Scope `files` to pages that actually MAKE the claim (e.g. compassion.html
is NOT in the patripassianism rule — it never says the Son was executed, so it needs no
fence; adding it would false-fire). Seeded conservatively; add a rule only after
confirming every listed file currently passes (node tools/check-required-fences.mjs).
A genuinely fence-free exception is accepted on-record in required-fences-baseline.json.

rules.what: Any surface arguing eternal generation must fence the Son against derived/later/lesser deity (the Arian direction).
rules.instead: Carry one of: 'co-equal and co-eternal' / 'in no way later or lesser' / 'an eternal relation of origin' / 'God from God' / 'begotten, not made'.

rules.what: Any surface saying the Son or God was crucified/executed must fence patripassianism: the Son suffered in his assumed human nature; the divine nature did not die and the Father was not crucified.
rules.instead: Fence with the two-natures / communicatio idiomatum point: the eternal Son suffered in the human nature he assumed; the divine nature did not die and the Father was not crucified.
